119: ### 5. Submodule Sync Commits (Parent Repository)
120: 
121: - **Title**: `chore(submodules): sync <submodule-name> with <descriptive-action>`
122:   - First line format: `chore(submodules): sync <submodule-name> with <action>`
123:   - Include a descriptive action that summarizes the changes
124: - **Short Summary**: `Updates <submodule-name> from <old-sha-short> to <new-sha-short> (<head-commit-title>)`
125: - **Full Metadata Body (MANDATORY)**: The body MUST contain the complete,
126:   structured industrial record of the submodule advance.
127: - **Changes Section Header**: `Changes (<submodule-name>) [<old-sha>..<new-sha>]:`
128:   - **Mandatory**: Use the full 40-character SHAs for both the previous pointer
129:     and the new pointer.
130:   - **Format**: Bullet points (`-`) listing commits in chronological order (older to newer)
131: - **Chronological Order**: The commit list MUST be ordered from **older to newer**.
132: - **Metadata Section Header**: `Metadata (<submodule-name>):`
133: - **Mandatory Fields**:
134:   - `Submodule: <name> -> <new-sha>`
135:   - `Submodule commit parent: <sha>`
136:     (merge: <parent1> <parent2> ← only if merge commit)
137:   - `Submodule commit msg: <title-line>`
138:   - `<body-paragraphs-if-multiline>`
139:   - `Submodule commit changes`: List paths and line counts (for the tip commit).
140:   - `Submodule commit author`: <name> <email>
141:   - `Submodule commit author time`: <timestamp>
142:   - `Submodule commit committer`: <name> <email>
143:   - `Submodule commit committer time`: <timestamp>
144: - **Registration URL**: Every sync commit MUST include the registration URL from
145:   `.gitmodules` at the end of the metadata block:
146:   `Register <submodule-name> submodule pointing to <registration-url>`
147: - **Content Summary**:
148:   - Body must list key changes introduced by the submodule update, based on
149:     the submodule's commit messages.
150:   - Do not include only the commit SHA; always summarize the actual changes.
151:   - Do not repeat information from the title in the body.
152: - **No Paraphrasing**: The submodule's original commit message body must be
153:   preserved without summarization or omission.
154: - **Format Consistency**: Use bullet points for all details, wrap lines at 72
155:   characters, follow all other formatting rules, and maintain standard
156:   imperative mood for the title.
157: 
158: #### 5.1 Huge-Range Bookend Variant (>500 commits)
159: 
160: When the submodule advance spans **more than 500 commits**, a flat
161: chronological listing becomes impractical (Git practical limits, reviewer
162: fatigue, log noise). In that case the agent MUST switch to the **bookend
163: variant**:
164: 
165: - **Changes Section Header**: still `Changes (<submodule-name>) [<old-sha>..<new-sha>] (N commits, bookend listing):` where `N` is the exact `git rev-list --count <old>..<new>` figure.
166: - **First-K bullets**: list the **oldest 10 commits** in chronological order.
167: - **Ellipsis line**: a single bullet `- ... (<N - 20> intermediate commits omitted; full list: \`git -C <submodule> log --oneline <old>..<new>\`)`.
168: - **Last-K bullets**: list the **newest 10 commits** in chronological order, ending with the tip commit.
169: - **Tip metadata block**: identical to the standard variant (parent, message, changes, author, committer, registration URL) — NEVER omitted.
170: - **Threshold**: 500 commits. Below the threshold, use the standard flat list. The threshold MUST be stated explicitly in the body via the `(N commits, bookend listing)` annotation so reviewers know why the list is abridged.
171: 
172: ### 6. Summarizing Opaque or Binary Changes
173: 
174: When changes involve files that Git identifies as binary (e.g., encoded text, large assets, database dumps), the agent

# OpenCode Session Problem-Solution-Workflow Analysis (v1)

## Composition Rationale

This skill is a **composer**: it does NOT re-implement YAML parsing or

1. **[`opencode-session-yaml-transcript-extractor`](../opencode-session-yaml-transcript-extractor/SKILL.md)** —

The composer's domain-specific value-add over the base alone: the
reconstruction procedure itself — reading the problem out of the user's
messages (incl. correction turns), locating the accepted solution, and
classifying tool sequences into accepted vs rejected paths — plus the

## 2. Operational Logic

### 2.1 The 7-step analysis procedure (Zero Omission)

1. **Locate the session's log files** — `.opencode/logs/ses_<id>/` per-turn
   directory (`000-header-*.yaml` + `NNN-<timestamp>.yaml`; filename order
   IS chronological) or the monolithic `ses_<id>.yaml`. Both layouts are
   accepted by `--input`.
2. **Extract the transcript** — run the base
   `extract-yaml-transcript.py` (via the composer script, or directly):
   one JSONL record per narrative element with global `index` and `turn`.
3. **Render the deterministic skeleton** — run
   `scripts/reconstruct-workflow.py --input <session> --output <report.md>`:
   session meta (id/title when present), `## 3. Workflow Executed` per-turn
   chronology (user text, thinking, tool calls with truncated args/results),
   per-turn tool-call summary table.
4. **Identify the Problem** (judgement) — read the user's textual messages:
   the FIRST message states the original ask; correction turns
   ("no, this is wrong", "yes - got it") mark rejected vs accepted states.
   Quote the exact user text that defines the problem.
5. **Identify the Solution** (judgement) — the state/answer the user
   ultimately accepts. Cite the concrete evidence path that produced it
   (DB key, file path, CLI command, output record).
6. **Classify the workflow** (judgement over the skeleton) — mark each
   tool-call prefix as accepted path or rejected/alternative path, using the
   thinking text and the correction turns as the boundary signal.
7. **Synthesize** — fill `## 1. Problem`, `## 2. Solution`,
   `## 4. Rejected / Alternative Paths`, `## 5. Final State` in the report;
   the `## 3. Workflow Executed` section is already deterministic.

### 2.2 Judgement guidance

- **Correction turns are the strongest signal**: a user message beginning
  with "no", "wrong", or restating the ask ("i want open editors. also all
  my editor tabs are pinned.") closes the previous attempt and re-opens the
  problem. The turn immediately AFTER the last correction carries the
  accepted direction.
- **The solution must be evidenced**: record the exact artifact that
  produced it (e.g. `state.vscdb` key `memento/workbench.parts.editor` →
  `editorpart.state.serializedGrid`, `sticky: N` = pinned count) — a
  solution without a path is an assertion, not an answer.
- **Rejected paths precede the correction**: a rejected path is a tool-call
  prefix that the thinking text abandons ("doesn't expose", "not persisted",
  "rejected path") or that a correction turn overrides.
- **Bound output size**: always pass `--truncate` (default 500) — full
  args/results must never be dumped to scrollback; the complete fidelity
  lives in the JSONL, not the report.

9: 
10: # Agent Planning Rule: Core Principles and Best Practices
11: 
12: This document outlines the mandatory planning protocol for all AI agents. The primary directive is to ensure all
13: actions are preceded by a transparent, user-approved plan. This rule is foundational to establishing a clear,
14: trustworthy, and effective interaction model.
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## 1. Goal Description & Versioning
19: 
20: All implementation plans MUST follow a strict naming and header convention to ensure traceability and version control.
21: 
22: - **H1 Header Versioning**: Every implementation plan MUST use the format `# [Goal Description] (vN)`
23:   as its primary H1 title (e.g., `# [Setup Authentication] (v1)`).
24: - **Rule Compliance Reference**: A dedicated section titled `## Rule Compliance Reference` MUST immediately follow the
25:   H1 header. It must contain a bulleted list of the specific industrial rules (with relative links) being followed in
26:   the current plan.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. The Core Planning Directive
31: 
32: All agents must present a clear, step-by-step plan before any implementation. The plan must be explicit,
33: actionable, and tailored to the user’s request. **Only after the plan is approved or clarified should
34: implementation begin.**
35: 
36: This directive is not merely a formality; it is a critical safeguard. By externalizing the planning process, the
37: agent minimizes the risk of misunderstanding, prevents "hallucination," and ensures complete alignment with the
38: user's intent from the outset.
39: 
40: ### 1.1 Primary Goal Persistence Mandate
41: 
42: The agent **MUST** carry over the original 'Starting Point' enquiry (the core objective) into every version of the
43: implementation plan. This goal must remain the primary heading of the document. Any shift in focus or addition of
44: sub-tasks MUST be explicitly documented as secondary or supporting actions to this primary goal, not as a replacement
45: for it.
46: 
47: ### 1.2 Architectural Boundary Verification
48: 
49: Before adding any execution step, the agent MUST verify it is not designated as 'CI/CD Managed' in project rules.
50: Local execution of automated pipeline tasks is PROHIBITED. If a script is for CI/CD, the agent must only modify its
51: templates or source metadata.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. Components of an Effective Plan
58: 
59: An effective plan is built on four key pillars:
60: 
61: - **Clarity:** The plan must be written in plain, unambiguous language. Avoid technical jargon or internal thought
62: 
63:     process descriptions. Each step should be a simple statement of intent, easily understood by a non-technical
64:     user.
65: 
66: - **Step-by-Step Breakdown:** The plan must break down the request into a logical sequence of discrete, manageable
67: 
68:     steps. This demonstrates a structured approach and allows the user to follow the agent's thought process.
69: 
70: - **Actionability:** Every step in the plan must represent a concrete, executable action. For example, instead of
71: 
72:     "Gather information," an actionable step would be "Search the web for Q4 2024 financial reports from Google."
73: 
74: - **Tailored to the Request:** The plan should directly address the specifics of the user's query. It should not be
75: 
76:     a generic template but a custom-designed workflow that reflects the unique nuances of the task.
77: 
78: ---
79: 
80: ## 4. The Agent Planning Workflow
81: 
82: A well-structured interaction with an agent should follow this five-step workflow:
83: 
84: 1. **Deconstruct the Request:** The agent's first internal action is to analyze the user's prompt. It should
85: 
86:    identify the core task, the specific constraints, the desired output format, and any potential ambiguities or
87:    missing information.
88: 
89: 1. **Formulate the Plan:** Based on the deconstruction, the agent constructs a detailed plan. This plan should be
90: 
91:    a bulleted or numbered list that outlines the exact steps to be taken, including any necessary data retrieval,
92:    analysis, or content generation.
93: 
94: 1. **Present for Approval**: The agent presents the formulated plan to the user. This is a crucial checkpoint.
95:    The agent should explicitly ask for confirmation or for any necessary adjustments before proceeding.
96:    - **Browser Approval**: For manual testing plans, all browser-based tool requests are considered pre-approved
97:        unless explicitly denied by the user.
98: 
99: 1. **Execute the Plan:** Upon receiving user approval, the agent proceeds to implement the plan, step by step. Each
100: 
101:    action is performed as outlined, ensuring the process remains transparent and predictable.
102: 
103: 1. **Report Progress & Completion:** The agent should provide a final summary of the work done, confirming that all
104: 
105:    steps in the plan were executed. For long or complex tasks, providing interim progress updates may also be
106:    beneficial.
107: 
108: ---
109: 
110: ## 5. Handling Edge Cases and Best Practices
111: 
112: - **Ambiguous Requests:** If the user's request is unclear or incomplete, the agent must include a clarification
113: 
114:     step in its plan. The plan should state, "First, I will ask for clarification on `the ambiguous part` to ensure I
115:     proceed correctly."
116: 
117: - **Multi-Turn Conversations:** For continuous dialogues, a new, explicit plan is required for each distinct task or
118: 
119:     significant shift in the user's request. Simple, short follow-up questions do not require a new plan.
120: 
121: - **Exemptions to the Rule:** A plan is not required for trivial, single-step requests that have a straightforward,
122: 
123:     factual answer. For example, a request like "What is the capital of France?" should be answered directly without
124:     a planning step. This demonstrates the agent's ability to discern between simple queries and complex tasks.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 6. Iterative Planning and Plan Versioning
129: 
130: The initial plan is a blueprint, not an unbreakable contract. For complex,
131: 
132: - **Categorical Alignment**: Group changes by their architectural layer (e.g., UI, Logic, Docs) unless they are
133: 
134:     functionally coupled.
135: 
136: - **Git Hygiene & Rebase Integration**: For tasks involving multiple branches or history refinement, the plan MUST
137: 
138:     include:
139: 
140: - **Hierarchical Mermaid Mapping**: Visualizing branch dependencies (referencing [Git Rebase Standardization
141: 
142:     Rules](./git-rebase-standardization-rules.md)).
143: 
144: - **CAM Table**: Mapping specific actions per commit to ensure logic isolation.
145: 
146: - **Workflow-First Priority**: If changes involve CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions, scripts), the agent **MUST** fix,
147: 
148:     test, and verify the workflow functionality *before* arranging or executing commits. Functional stability of the
149:     CI pipeline takes precedence over documentation or stylistic refinements.
150: 
151: ### 1.1 Long-Running & Dynamic Tasks
152: 
153: For long-running or dynamic tasks, the agent may encounter new information or unforeseen obstacles that necessitate
154: a change in direction. In these cases, the agent MUST NOT deviate from the original plan without explicit approval.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 7. Industrial Planning Mandates
159: 
160: - **Environment State Check**: Every plan involving runtime verification MUST include a prerequisite step to
161:     confirm the application is running and accessible (e.g., "Verify App is live at `http://localhost:3000`").
162: - **Maximum Literal Detail**: Plans must be exhaustive and literal.
163: 
164: ### 5.1 Impact Scan Enhancement (Maximum Literal Detail)
165: 
166: For every DELETION, RENAMING, or REFUNDAMENTAL change, the plan MUST include a dedicated 'Surface Area Scan' to identify
167: and remediate all global references, internal links, and cross-file dependencies.
168: 
169: ### 5.2 Anti-Summarization & No-Truncation Guardrail
170:

Three failure modes have been observed when authors append rows carelessly: 521: 522: 1. **Unrelated skills listed**: a skill that neither composes nor consumes the base is added because its topic sounded adjacent. PROHIBITED — the table loses signal and downstream readers compose the wrong primitive. 523: 2. **Merely related skills listed**: a sibling skill that shares a topic but does NOT invoke / depend on / extend the base is added. PROHIBITED in this table — such skills belong in the base's `## Related Skills` section instead. The Composition table is reserved for true composers (callers that pipe through the base's public contract) and consumers (skills that hard-depend on the base's output shape). 524: 3. **Generic / non-contextual descriptions**: a true composer is listed but its description is a paraphrase of the composer's own one-liner ("does X with Y"). 678: ### 5.6 Cross-Reference Link Discipline
679: 
680: Every **first-mention** (within a given section / subsection) of any of the following inside a skill doc MUST be rendered as a proper relative markdown link, not as a bare backtick code span:
681: 
682: - A sibling skill folder → `[`<skill-name>`](../<skill-name>/SKILL.md)`
683: - A rule doc → `[`<rule-name>.md`](../../../ai-agent-rules/<rule-name>.md)` (path depth adjusts to the host file's location)
684: - A memory file → `[`<memory>.md`](../../../memories/repo/<memory>.md)`
685: - Any other in-repo path the reader may want to navigate to
686: 
687: Subsequent re-mentions within the same section/subsection MAY use a bare backtick code span (`` `name` ``) for readability — but the FIRST mention sets the navigability anchor for that section.
688: 
689: **Rationale**: a skill doc is read as a hypertext, not a manuscript. A bare `` `repo-scratch-output-capture` `` looks identical to a linked one in the source but is dead text in the rendered view — readers cannot navigate to the referenced skill and authors of inbound links lose discoverability of their target.
690: 
691: **Forbidden patterns** (must be fixed when found):
692: 
693: 1. A skill name mentioned in prose as a bare code span when the host skill is not itself the named skill.
694: 2. A relative path written as `\`../foo/SKILL.md\`` (code span containing a path) without being wrapped as a link.
695: 3. A `§N` citation that names a foreign skill without linking to that skill's SKILL.md.
696: 
697: **Verification step** (mandatory before declaring a skill-doc edit done):
698: 
699: ```bash
700: grep -nE '`[a-z][a-z0-9_./-]+`' path/to/SKILL.md
701: ```
702: 
703: Read every hit and ask: is the backticked token a skill folder, rule doc, memory file, or repo path? If YES and the same line does NOT contain the surrounding `[…](…)` link syntax → convert to a proper relative link. Acceptable bare-code-span backticked tokens: shell commands, code identifiers (function/variable/class names), file extensions, CLI flags, sentinel strings.

707: ### 5.7 Heading Scope Discipline (Choose a Parent That Hosts Siblings)
708: 
709: Before naming a new top-level section (`## N. <Heading>`) in a skill doc, the author MUST ask: *"Is this a single atomic concern, or is it one of multiple related concerns that share a theme?"*
710: 
711: If **multiple related concerns** are foreseeable → choose a parent heading whose scope is **broad enough to host current and future siblings**, and place the immediate concern as a `### N.1` subsection under it. Do NOT promote the first specific concern to top-level — doing so forces later authors to either (a) cram unrelated concerns under a too-narrow heading, or (b) renumber the whole document when a sibling arrives.
712: 
713: **Decision test** (apply before writing the heading):
714: 
715: 1. Can you imagine writing one or more sibling `### N.M` sections on the same theme within the next 1–3 authoring sessions? → **YES** → the parent (theme) is the correct top-level; the concern is `### N.1`.
716: 2. Is this section genuinely atomic and stands alone with no foreseeable siblings on the same theme? → **YES** → a specific top-level is fine.
717: 3. If unsure → prefer the broader parent. A parent with only one subsection is cheap to maintain; a misplaced top-level is expensive to restructure later (every cross-reference to `§N` breaks under renumbering).
718: 
719: **Forbidden patterns**:
720: 
721: 1. **Premature specificity**: making `## N. <Specific Concern>` when 2+ sibling concerns on the same theme are visible at authoring time.
722: 2. **Retroactive umbrella-stuffing**: when a sibling concern arises later, cramming it under a too-narrow existing top-level instead of restructuring to the correct parent. PROHIBITED — restructure to the correct parent and renumber inbound references per §5.1.

728: ### 5.8 Style-Consistency Discipline (Match the Surrounding Document)
729: 
730: Before adding or editing any block in an existing skill doc, the author MUST sample the surrounding 20–50 lines AND the document's overall conventions, and ensure the new content matches the dominant local pattern across **all** of the following axes:
731: 
732: | Axis | Examples of variants to choose between |
733: | --- | --- |
734: | List marker | `-` vs `*` vs `1.` (numbered) |
735: | List indentation depth | 2-space vs 4-space continuation |
736: | Blank lines around headings | 0, 1, or 2 blank lines above/below `##` / `###` |
737: | Blank lines between list items | none vs one (compact vs loose lists) |
738: | Blank lines around fenced code | always one above + one below vs flush |
739: | Bold / italic markers | `**bold**` vs `__bold__`; `*italic*` vs `_italic_` |
740: | Code-span vs link for skill/file names | governed by §5.6 (Cross-Reference Link Discipline) |
741: | Horizontal-rule pattern | `***` vs `---` vs none; frequency between sections |
742: | Step / mandate prefix | `1.`, `**1.**`, `### N.M`, `**Mandate Name**:` |
743: | Table header alignment | `:---` vs `---` vs `---:` |
744: | Heading capitalization | Title Case vs Sentence case |
745: 
746: **Mandates**:
747: 
748: 1. **Sample before write.** Read at least the immediate predecessor + successor sibling sections of the insertion point. Match their dominant style. If conflicting styles already coexist locally, match the nearest sibling at the same nesting depth.
749: 2. **Do not introduce a second marker style.** If the document uses `-` for bullets throughout, do NOT introduce a `*` bullet block. If parent sections use `**Mandate Name**:` prefix, do NOT introduce a bare numbered list inside a new sibling sub-section.
750: 3. **Preserve indentation depth.** If continuation lines under a list item use 4 spaces in the surrounding document, the new content's continuation lines MUST also use 4 spaces — not 2.
751: 4. **Preserve blank-line spacing.** Count blank lines above/below the nearest sibling heading and reproduce the same count for the new heading.
752:

754: the [`list-indent-consistency`](../general/list-indent-consistency/SKILL.md)
755: base skill.

759: ```bash

761: ```
762: 
763: Visually scan the diff for style drift vs surrounding lines: do the inserted bullets use the same marker as the file's existing bullets? Same indentation? Same blank-line padding around headings? If any axis drifts → fix in the same edit, not later.

778: ### 6.1 Gap Analysis

8: # Git Submodule Pointer Repair Skill (v1)
9: 
10: This skill provide surgical, high-fidelity repair of invalid submodule pointers within a parent repository's history. It
11: implements the **Synchronization Horizon** algorithm to autonomously identify the correct architectural alignment point

13: 
14: ***
15: 
16: ## 1. Environment & Dependencies
17: 
18: The agent MUST verify the following tools are available before execution:
19: 
20: - **Git**: Mandatory for repository operations.
21: - **Python 3**: Mandatory for the `repair.py` synchronization engine.
22: 
23: ```bash
24: # Verify environment
25: which git && git --version
26: which python3 && python3 --version
27: ```
28: 
29: ***
30: 
31: ## 2. Operational Logic: The Synchronization Horizon
32: 
33: This algorithm identifies the exact architectural alignment point ($s_p$) where parent repository mandates are satisfied
34: by submodule history.
35: 
36: ### 2.1 Detection & Backtracking (The Discovery)
37: 1. **Identify Target**: Locate submodules with invalid pointers in the input Parent SHA.
38: 2. **Verify Validity**: For every invalid pointer, backtrack in the parent history to find the **Last Known Valid SHA**.
39: 3. **Isolate Intro Commit**: The commit that changed the last known valid SHA to the first invalid SHA is the **Invalid
40:   Reference Introduction Commit**.
41: 
42: ### 2.2 Cumulative Synchronization Scan (Mapping)
43: 1. **Extract Mandates**: Retrieve the commit message of the **Invalid Reference Introduction Commit**.
44: 2. **Successor Analysis**: Identify the successor commits ($s_1, s_2, \dots, s_n$) of the Last Known Valid SHA in the
45:   submodule repository.
46: 3. **Iterative Alignment**: Analyze the cumulative changes $\{s_1 \dots s_i\}$. 
47: 4. **Identify Boundary $s_p$**: The loop stops at $s_p$ where the cumulative changes correctly and completely satisfy
48:   the parent's mandates ($s_{p+1}$ MUST be unrelated drift).
49: 
50: ### 2.3 Surgical Repair (Execution)
51: 1. **Safety Backup**: MUST create a backup tag before modification (e.g., `backup-pointer-repair-<timestamp>`).
52: 2. **Pointer Swap**: Surgically edit the **Invalid Reference Introduction Commit**, replacing the invalid hash with
53:   $s_p$.
54: 3. **Propagation**: Propagate the fix across subsequent history using a non-interactive rebase or equivalent
55:   transformation.
56: 
57: ***
58: 
59: ## 3. Cleanup Protocol
60: 
61: The safety backup tag MUST be managed with 100% human-in-the-loop fidelity.
62: 
63: 1. **Verification**: Confirm `ls-tree` at the sync point reflects $s_p$.
64: 2. **Authorization**: Explicitly ask the user: *"History repair verified. May I delete the safety backup tag
65:   <tag_name>?"*
66: 3. **Execution**: Delete the tag ONLY upon explicit "yes" confirmation.
67: 
68: ***
69: 
70: ## 4. Automation Engine
71: 
72: The surgical logic is encapsulated in the industrial Python engine:
73: [scripts/repair.py](./scripts/repair.py)
74: 
75: ```bash
76: # Example Usage:
77: python3 .agents/skills/git-submodule-pointer-repair/scripts/repair.py --parent <SHA> --submodule <PATH>
78: ```
79: 
80: ***
81: 
82: ## 5. Mass Pointer Reconciliation (Full History Rewrite Recovery)
83: 
84: Use this protocol when the **entire submodule history has been rewritten** (e.g., linearized, rebased, pruned), making
85: **every historical pointer** in the parent repository invalid.
86: 
87: ### 5.1 Scope Assessment
88: 
89: ```bash
90: # List ALL parent commits touching the submodule pointer, oldest → newest
91: git log --reverse --format="%H | %as | %s" -- <submodule-path>
92: ```
93: 
94: Save this list. Each entry has an invalid pointer that needs a verified replacement.
95: 
96: ### 5.2 Build the Verified Mapping
97: 
98: For each invalid pointer SHA, find its counterpart in the refined submodule history using **high-fidelity metadata
99: extraction** (per the `git_commit_metadata_extraction` skill).
100: 
101: #### 5.2.0 Match-Key Selection (CRITICAL)
102: 
103: The match key MUST be chosen based on **how the submodule history was rewritten**:

105: | Submodule rewrite type | Recommended match key | Subject (`%s`) safe to include? |
106: | --- | --- | --- |
107: | Cherry-pick / linearize / rebase **without** message edits | `%aI \| %ae \| %s \| sorted-file-list` | ✅ Yes — strongest key |
108: | **Message-only reword** (e.g., via [`git-commit-message-reword`](../git-commit-message-reword/SKILL.md) or [`git-commit-message-bulk-reword`](../git-commit-message-bulk-reword/SKILL.md)) | `%aI \| %ae \| sorted-file-list` (subject EXCLUDED) | ❌ **NO** — reworded subjects will not match; including `%s` produces false negatives |
109: | Mixed (some commits reworded, some not) | `%aI \| %ae \| sorted-file-list` (subject EXCLUDED) — uniformly | ❌ NO |
110: | Squash / split (commits collapsed or divided) | This skill is INSUFFICIENT — a 1:1 mapping does not exist; consult the user for manual N:1 / 1:N decisions | N/A |

10: # Planning Artifact Naming Convention (v1)
11: 
12: This skill defines the naming convention for all planning artifacts
13: generated during AI-agent sessions. The convention embeds session
14: identity (human-readable name + machine-readable ID) directly into

20: 
21: ***
22: 
23: ## 1. Formula
24: 
25: ```text
26: docs/<date>_<session-id>_<session-name-slug>_<artifact-type>_v<version>.md
27: ```

39: | `session-name-slug` | Always | Kebab-case of the opencode session name | `opencode-config-versioning-preservation` |

42: | Extension | Always | `.md` | `.md` |
43: 
44: ### 1.2 Separator Rule
45: 
46: - **Underscore** (`_`) separates every top-level part.
47: - **Hyphen** (`-`) is used only WITHIN a part (date-separator,
48: session-name-slug, artifact-type).

68: ### 1.3 `ses_` Prefix Handling

71: 2. **Check Path**:

73:     ```bash
74:     PAGER=cat git config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp path | grep "<OWNER_REPO_PATH>"
75:     ```
76: 
77:     - If the path already exists, **HALT**.
78: 
79: ### 3.2 Initial Addition
80: 
81: > [!IMPORTANT]
82: > **Industrial Mandate**: Submodules MUST be added and initialized **one by one**. Do NOT
83: > chain multiple additions in a single command. This ensures atomic failure detection and
84: > prevents configuration corruption.
85: 
86: ```bash
87: # Add the submodule at the derived path
88: git submodule add <URL> <OWNER_REPO_PATH>
89: ```
90: 
91: - **Pedagogical Breakdown**:
92:     - `add`: Registers the new submodule in `.gitmodules`.
93:     - `<URL>`: The source repository.
94:     - `<OWNER_REPO_PATH>`: The target directory (e.g., `owner_repo`).
95: 
96: ### 3.3 Initialization & Synchronization
97: 
98: ```bash
99: # Initialize ONLY the just-added submodule and fetch its data, including any nested
100: # submodules it carries. The trailing path scopes the operation so it stays atomic
101: # with the one-by-one mandate from §3.2.
102: PAGER=cat git submodule update --init --recursive <OWNER_REPO_PATH>
103: ```
104: 
105: - **Pedagogical Breakdown**:
106:     - `--init`: Initializes the submodule in `.git/config` if not already present.
107:     - `--recursive`: **Mandatory.** Submodules frequently embed their own submodules (the
108:       `powershell-scripts` submodule of `ai-agent-rules` is a real example). Omitting
109:       `--recursive` leaves nested pointers uninitialized and silently breaks any script
110:       that depends on them.
111:     - `<OWNER_REPO_PATH>`: Scopes init to the path just added in §3.2, preserving
112:       atomic failure detection.
113: 
114: #### 3.3.1 Fresh-Clone Bootstrap
115: 
116: When the **parent** repository is being cloned for the first time (not when a single
117: submodule is being added to an existing checkout), use the recursive clone form so every
118: level of the submodule tree materializes in one command:
119: 
120: ```bash
121: git clone --recurse-submodules <PARENT_REPO_URL>
122: # or, on an already-cloned parent that is missing submodule contents:
123: PAGER=cat git submodule update --init --recursive
124: ```
125: 
126: The agent MUST use the recursive form unconditionally — the cost of an unnecessary
127: recursion is negligible, while the cost of a missing nested submodule is a silent
128: runtime failure later.
129: 
130: ### 3.4 Branch Tracking Enforcement (Critical)
131: 
132: Per `git-submodule-rules.md`, the agent MUST NOT leave the submodule in a "detached HEAD" state.
133: 
134: 1. **Enter the Submodule**: `cd <OWNER_REPO_PATH>`
135: 2. **Identify Default Branch**: Run `git remote show origin | grep "HEAD branch" | cut -d ":" -f 2 | xargs` or assume
136: `main`/`master` based on inspection.
137: 3. **Checkout Branch**:
138: 
139:     ```bash
140:     git checkout main # or master, based on discovery
141:     git pull origin main
142:     ```
143: 
144: 4. **Return to Root**: `cd ..`
145: 
146: ***
147: 
148: ## 4. Verification & Commit Preparation
149: 
150: 1. **Verify Status**: Run `git status` to confirm the addition and pointer change.
151: 2. **Propose Commit**: Follow the atomic commit standard.
152:     - Message: `feat(submodule): add <OWNER_REPO_PATH> submodule`
153:     - Include: URL and purpose.

10: # Agent Planning Rule: Core Principles and Best Practices
11: 
12: This document outlines the mandatory planning protocol for all AI agents. The primary directive is to ensure all
13: actions are preceded by a transparent, user-approved plan. This rule is foundational to establishing a clear,
14: trustworthy, and effective interaction model.
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## 1. Goal Description & Versioning
19: 
20: All implementation plans MUST follow a strict naming and header convention to ensure traceability and version control.
21: 
22: - **H1 Header Versioning**: Every implementation plan MUST use the format `# [Goal Description] (vN)`
23:   as its primary H1 title (e.g., `# [Setup Authentication] (v1)`).
24: - **Rule Compliance Reference**: A dedicated section titled `## Rule Compliance Reference` MUST immediately follow the
25:   H1 header. It must contain a bulleted list of the specific industrial rules (with relative links) being followed in
26:   the current plan.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. The Core Planning Directive
31: 
32: All agents must present a clear, step-by-step plan before any implementation. The plan must be explicit,
33: actionable, and tailored to the user’s request. **Only after the plan is approved or clarified should
34: implementation begin.**
35: 
36: This directive is not merely a formality; it is a critical safeguard. By externalizing the planning process, the
37: agent minimizes the risk of misunderstanding, prevents "hallucination," and ensures complete alignment with the
38: user's intent from the outset.
39: 
40: ### 1.1 Primary Goal Persistence Mandate
41: 
42: The agent **MUST** carry over the original 'Starting Point' enquiry (the core objective) into every version of the
43: implementation plan. This goal must remain the primary heading of the document. Any shift in focus or addition of
44: sub-tasks MUST be explicitly documented as secondary or supporting actions to this primary goal, not as a replacement
45: for it.
46: 
47: ### 1.2 Architectural Boundary Verification
48: 
49: Before adding any execution step, the agent MUST verify it is not designated as 'CI/CD Managed' in project rules.
50: Local execution of automated pipeline tasks is PROHIBITED. If a script is for CI/CD, the agent must only modify its
51: templates or source metadata.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. Components of an Effective Plan
58: 
59: An effective plan is built on four key pillars:
60: 
61: - **Clarity:** The plan must be written in plain, unambiguous language. Avoid technical jargon or internal thought
62: 
63:     process descriptions. Each step should be a simple statement of intent, easily understood by a non-technical
64:     user.
65: 
66: - **Step-by-Step Breakdown:** The plan must break down the request into a logical sequence of discrete, manageable
67: 
68:     steps. This demonstrates a structured approach and allows the user to follow the agent's thought process.
69: 
70: - **Actionability:** Every step in the plan must represent a concrete, executable action. For example, instead of
71: 
72:     "Gather information," an actionable step would be "Search the web for Q4 2024 financial reports from Google."
73: 
74: - **Tailored to the Request:** The plan should directly address the specifics of the user's query. It should not be
75: 
76:     a generic template but a custom-designed workflow that reflects the unique nuances of the task.
77: 
78: ---
79: 
80: ## 4. The Agent Planning Workflow
81: 
82: A well-structured interaction with an agent should follow this five-step workflow:
83: 
84: 1. **Deconstruct the Request:** The agent's first internal action is to analyze the user's prompt. It should
85: 
86:    identify the core task, the specific constraints, the desired output format, and any potential ambiguities or
87:    missing information.
88: 
89: 1. **Formulate the Plan:** Based on the deconstruction, the agent constructs a detailed plan. This plan should be
90: 
91:    a bulleted or numbered list that outlines the exact steps to be taken, including any necessary data retrieval,
92:    analysis, or content generation.
93: 
94: 1. **Present for Approval**: The agent presents the formulated plan to the user. This is a crucial checkpoint.
95:    The agent should explicitly ask for confirmation or for any necessary adjustments before proceeding.
96:    - **Browser Approval**: For manual testing plans, all browser-based tool requests are considered pre-approved
97:        unless explicitly denied by the user.
98: 
99: 1. **Execute the Plan:** Upon receiving user approval, the agent proceeds to implement the plan, step by step. Each
100: 
101:    action is performed as outlined, ensuring the process remains transparent and predictable.
102: 
103: 1. **Report Progress & Completion:** The agent should provide a final summary of the work done, confirming that all
104: 
105:    steps in the plan were executed. For long or complex tasks, providing interim progress updates may also be
106:    beneficial.
107: 
108: ---
109: 
110: ## 5. Handling Edge Cases and Best Practices
111: 
112: - **Ambiguous Requests:** If the user's request is unclear or incomplete, the agent must include a clarification
113: 
114:     step in its plan. The plan should state, "First, I will ask for clarification on `the ambiguous part` to ensure I
115:     proceed correctly."
116: 
117: - **Multi-Turn Conversations:** For continuous dialogues, a new, explicit plan is required for each distinct task or
118: 
119:     significant shift in the user's request. Simple, short follow-up questions do not require a new plan.
120: 
121: - **Exemptions to the Rule:** A plan is not required for trivial, single-step requests that have a straightforward,
122: 
123:     factual answer. For example, a request like "What is the capital of France?" should be answered directly without
124:     a planning step. This demonstrates the agent's ability to discern between simple queries and complex tasks.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 6. Iterative Planning and Plan Versioning
129: 
130: The initial plan is a blueprint, not an unbreakable contract. For complex,
131: 
132: - **Categorical Alignment**: Group changes by their architectural layer (e.g., UI, Logic, Docs) unless they are
133: 
134:     functionally coupled.
135: 
136: - **Git Hygiene & Rebase Integration**: For tasks involving multiple branches or history refinement, the plan MUST
137: 
138:     include:
139: 
140: - **Hierarchical Mermaid Mapping**: Visualizing branch dependencies (referencing [Git Rebase Standardization
141: 
142:     Rules](./git-rebase-standardization-rules.md)).
143: 
144: - **CAM Table**: Mapping specific actions per commit to ensure logic isolation.
145: 
146: - **Workflow-First Priority**: If changes involve CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions, scripts), the agent **MUST** fix,
147: 
148:     test, and verify the workflow functionality *before* arranging or executing commits. Functional stability of the
149:     CI pipeline takes precedence over documentation or stylistic refinements.
150: 
151: ### 1.1 Long-Running & Dynamic Tasks
152: 
153: For long-running or dynamic tasks, the agent may encounter new information or unforeseen obstacles that necessitate
154: a change in direction. In these cases, the agent MUST NOT deviate from the original plan without explicit approval.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 7. Industrial Planning Mandates
159: 
160: - **Environment State Check**: Every plan involving runtime verification MUST include a prerequisite step to
161:     confirm the application is running and accessible (e.g., "Verify App is live at `http://localhost:3000`").
162: - **Maximum Literal Detail**: Plans must be exhaustive and literal.
163: 
164: ### 5.1 Impact Scan Enhancement (Maximum Literal Detail)
165: 
166: For every DELETION, RENAMING, or REFUNDAMENTAL change, the plan MUST include a dedicated 'Surface Area Scan' to identify
167: and remediate all global references, internal links, and cross-file dependencies.
168: 
169: ### 5.2 Anti-Summarization & No-Truncation Guardrail
170: 
171: Agents MUST NOT summarize or collapse previously established literal details (file lists, exact commands, logic
172: branches) unless they are functionally obsolete or a mistake. Maximum clarity and non-ambiguity take precedence over
173: brevity. **The 'Change History' table MUST NOT be truncated.** It must remain a complete and literal record of all plan
174: versions (v1, v2, v3, ... vN) without omission.
175: 
176: - **Files:** Explicitly list every file (absolute paths) to be created, modified, or deleted.
177: - **Exact Commands:** CLI commands must be written exactly as they will be executed, including full arguments and piped
178:     operations.
179: - **Literal Payloads:** For operations like `git commit --amend -m "..."`, the plan must include the **literal message
180:     string** within the execution step, not just a reference to it.
181: - **Verifications:** Explicitly state the exact command or visual check used to verify each step.
182: - **Guardrails**: Restate the literal logic for handling conflicts, empty commits, and safety checks in every iteration.
183: - **Pre-Plan Context Gathering**: Information gathering (reading files, `git diff`,`ls`) must happen **BEFORE**
184:     the plan is finalized. A plan based on assumptions is a failed plan.
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 8. Temporal Hygiene & Change History
189: 
190: To ensure absolute traceability and industrial reliability, all planning and verification artifacts MUST
191: incorporate temporal data.
192: 
193: - **Execution Timestamps**: Every item in `task.md` and `walkthrough.md` MUST include a completion or event
194:     timestamp in the format `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm]`.
195: - **Change History Table**: Every versioned implementation plan (v2+) MUST include a "Change History" table
196:     immediately following the goal statement. This table MUST track:
197: 
198:     | Timestamp | Summary of Changes | Rationale |
199:     | :--- | :--- | :--- |
200:     | `[YYYY-DD-MM HH:mm]` | Concise description of the delta. | Why the change was necessary. |
201: 
202: ---
203: 
204: ## 9. Plan Versioning & SSOT Integrity (History Mandate)
205: 
206: **Iterative Planning** is the process of updating a plan based on new findings or changes in a task's requirements.
207: This practice ensures flexibility while maintaining the core principles of transparency and user alignment.
208: 
209: - **Plan Versioning**: All plans must be explicitly versioned (e.g., `implementation_plan_v1.md`, `implementation_plan_v2.md`).
210: - **History Mandate**: New versions MUST NOT overwrite old versions. Each new version MUST include the Change History table documenting all previous revisions.
211: - **SSOT (Single Source of Truth)**: Each version MUST be self-contained, restating all valid context and guardrails. Do not refer to previous versions for "missing details."
212: - **Fresh Start Protocol**: When a "Fresh Start" version (vN) is declared, all subsequent plans (vN+1, vN+2, etc.) MUST reset the 'Change History' and 'User Questions & Answers' to only include items from the declared fresh start version onwards. This is a strict exception to the full history mandate.
213: 
214: ### 7.1 Continuity Audit Mandate (CAM)
215: 
216: Before presenting a new plan version, the agent **MUST** perform a literal line-by-line comparison against the previous
217: version. Any dropped task, alert, or requirement MUST be either restored or explicitly listed in the 'Change History'
218: with a rationale for its removal. **Summarizing integrated logic from sub-plans is a violation.**
219: 
220: **Verbatim-Superset Construction:** When creating version n of ANY versioned artifact (plan, preview, walkthrough,
221: audit-log, summary, skill doc, release notes), the new version MUST be version n-1's text kept verbatim, with version
222: n's deltas appended — never rewritten, reworded, reordered, or selectively dropped (even with a Change History
223: rationale). Rationale entries in the Change History explain deltas; they do not license removal of previous content.
224: The deterministic construction is operationalized by the
225: `versioned-artifact-superset-build` base skill
226: (`scripts/build-version-superset.py`); the `planning-version-coverage-audit`
227: audit verifies the result post-hoc.
228: 
229: ### 7.2 Sub-Plan Versioning & Integration Mandate
230: 
231: All planning artifacts, including secondary or 'sub-plans,' MUST follow the versioning mandate (v1, v2, etc.). They
232: MUST NOT be edited in place. Once a sub-plan is confirmed by the user, its content MUST be integrated into the next
233: version of the main implementation plan while maintaining its full literal detail. **All subsequent updates MUST occur
234: within the main plan.** **Integration MUST be via literal copy-paste of all confirmed mandates.** Any modification for
235: 'brevity' is prohibited. Once integrated, the sub-plan is retired and redundant versioning is forbidden.
236: 
237: - **Propose a Plan Revision:** When a change is required, the agent must immediately pause execution
238:   and present a revised plan to the user.
239: - **Provide a Rationale:** The agent must clearly explain **why** the change is necessary.
240: - **Seek Approval:** The agent must explicitly ask for user approval for the revised plan before proceeding.
241:   This final check ensures the new direction aligns with the user's updated expectations.
242: 
243: ---
244: 
245: ## 10. Task Artifact Synchronization
246: 
247: Follow the status markers and include timestamps:
248: 
249: - **Initial Creation**: Create `task.md` at the start of planning with all top-level items.
250: - **Incremental Updates**: Update `task.md` after completing each significant milestone.
251: - **Status Markers**: Use `[ ]` for pending, `[/]` for in-progress, and `[x]` for completed items `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm]`.
252: - **Artifact Location**: All planning artifacts (task.md, implementation plans, walkthroughs) MUST be stored in
253:     the **main repository's** `docs/` directory (e.g., `docs/implementation-plans/<date>-<topic>.md`). When
254:     `ai-agent-rules/` is a Git submodule, artifacts MUST NOT be placed inside the submodule — doing so scatters
255:     planning history into a separate repo's commit graph. The main repo's `docs/` tree is the single source of
256:     truth for all planning artifacts.
257: - **Artifact Cleanup**: If everything is OK, we can remove the artifacts. The removal needs explicit user confirmation.
258: - **Compliance Mandate**: Every generated artifact (task, implementation plan, walkthrough) MUST strictly comply
259:     with **[Markdown Generation Skill](https://github.com/baneeishaque/ai-suite/blob/3786486bb54805fde12181bc8db34aaabede3e92/.agents/skills/markdown-generation/SKILL.md)** and
260:     **[Markdown Generation Rules Additions](./markdown-generation-rules-additions.md)**.
261:     This includes mandatory verification using `markdownlint-cli` before finalizing any artifact.
262: 
263: ---
264: 
265: ## 11. Status Traceability in Iterative Plans
266: 
267: To ensure absolute clarity during multi-phase execution, iterative plans (v2+) MUST track the status of proposed changes.
268: 
269: - **Marking Completed Steps**: If an implementation plan is updated during execution, any proposed change that has
270:   already been successfully implemented MUST be explicitly marked as `[DONE] [YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm]` or
271:   `[COMPLETED] [YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm]` within the 'Proposed Changes' section.
272: - **Visual Distinction**: Completed steps should ideally remain in the plan (to maintain context) but be clearly
273:   demarcated to differentiate them from pending work.
274: 
275: ---
276: 
277: ## 11. User Question Integration Mandate
278: 
279: To ensure maximum transparency and technical accuracy, the agent MUST explicitly address any technical or
280: process-related questions raised by the user during the planning phase.
281: 
282: - **Mandated Documentation**: All user questions and their corresponding agent answers MUST be documented in a
283:     dedicated **"User Questions & Answers"** section at the top of the revised implementation plan.
284: - **Traceability**: This ensures that critical clarifications and course corrections are captured in the
285:     Single Source of Truth (SSOT), making them available for future reference and audits.
286: - **Clarity**: Answers should be technically precise, referring to specific rules or protocols where applicable.
287: 
288: ---
289: 
290: ## 12. State-Dependent Phase Gating
291: 
292: Plans involving future states (e.g., Git history after 3 phases of changes)
293: **MUST NOT** predict or mock the result. They must instead define a **Protocol
294: Gate**: a set of mandatory discovery commands (e.g., `git status`, `git diff`)
295: and verification steps that the agent will run *at that time* to generate a
296: fresh, accurate preview for user approval.
297: 
298: ---
299: 
300: ## 13. Sequential Objective Protocol
301: 
302: To ensure absolute precision and user control, the agent MUST adhere to a strict sequential focus:
303: 
304: - **Single Objective Focus**: When instructed to perform a specific task (e.g., "update rules"), the agent MUST focus
305:   solely on that objective.
306: - **Deferment of Follow-ups**: The agent MUST NOT plan or prepare for follow-up actions (e.g., commit execution) in
307:   the same plan unless explicitly asked.
308: - **Verification Gates**: Follow-up instructions will be provided by the user *after* the current objective is
309:   confirmed complete.
310: - **Instructional Rationale**: When told to update rules, focus on updates ONLY. Do not jump to execution or
311:   downstream tasks until explicitly directed.
312: 
313: ## 14. Single Source of Truth & Content Integrity
314: 
315: The agent MUST strictly maintain the integrity of existing documentation:
316: 
317: - **Anti-Duplication**: Please don't duplicate things. We always need SSOT.
318: - **Audit Requirement**: When adding or updating something, the agent MUST read the file deeply and carefully. Only add what is missing.
319: - **Blending Strategy**: Blend new information into the existing documentation, or enhance the existing information. We always need single source.

9: # AI Agent Rule Standard Creation
10: 
11: This document defines the craftsmanship standards for creating new AI Agent Rules. Adhering to these protocols ensures

44: ## 2. File Naming & Meta-Data
45: 
46: All rule files must be stored in the `AI-Agent-Rules` directory. However, for specific workflows,
47: tasks, or capabilities, the system mandates a **Skill-First** architecture.
48: 
49: - **Skill-First Architecture**: Any new, complex work process or agent-specific workflow
50:   MUST be created as an **Agent Skill** instead of a flat rule file. Rationale: rules /
51:   instruction files are **vendor-locked** (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
52:   `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.windsurfrules`, etc.) -- a rule authored for one vendor is invisible
53:   to every other. The Agent Skills standard ([agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io),
54:   Anthropic-originated, multi-vendor adopted) is the open, portable alternative: a single
55:   `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter is consumable by every conformant runtime. Authoring a
56:   parallel rule file alongside a skill is **FORBIDDEN** -- it re-introduces vendor lock and
57:   splits the SSOT. Full rationale: see `rule-to-skill-industrialization` skill (sibling
58:   `ai-agents` repo).
59: - **Skill Directory**: Skills are housed in `.agent/skills/<skill-name>/` (legacy/single-agent) or
60:   `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/` (plural/standardized). Skill names MUST use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (no underscores).
61: - **Core Skill Files**:
62:     - `SKILL.md`: The SSOT containing active instructions following the **agentskills.io protocol**
63:       (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body).
64:     - `AGENTS.md`: The companion bridge providing "passive context" and referring tools back to the `SKILL.md`.
65: - **Independence Mandate**: Every Skill MUST be self-contained. It MUST manage its own environmental verification,
66:   dependencies, and execution logic independently.
67: - **Layered Composition Mandate (Base → Composer)**: When a workflow contains a generic primitive (e.g., glob assembly,
68:   metadata extraction, path normalization) reused by multiple domain-specific tasks, it MUST be split into:
69:     1. A **base skill** that owns ONLY the generic primitive, accepts inputs via stdin / file / arguments, and
70:        produces a deterministic output. The base skill MUST be domain-agnostic.
71:     2. One or more **composer skills** that own the domain-specific discovery (e.g., parsing `.gitmodules`, walking
72:        `node_modules`) and pipe their output into the base skill via its public CLI contract.
73:   Composer scripts MUST resolve the base script through a relative path (`$(dirname "$0")/../../<base>/scripts/...`)
74:   so the pipeline works regardless of the caller's `cwd`. Inlining base logic into a composer is **FORBIDDEN** —
75:   duplication breaks the SSOT contract and silently diverges bug fixes. Each composer's `SKILL.md` MUST link to its
76:   base skill in a "Composition Rationale" section, and the base skill MUST list known composers in a "Composition by
77:   Higher-Level Skills" section so the dependency graph is bidirectionally discoverable.
78: - **Path Portability**: All links within a Skill MUST be relative and depth-correct (e.g., `../../../` for
79:   skills residing 3 levels deep) to ensure zero-dependency portability across filesystems.

81:   also consumed as a Git submodule of another repository (e.g., `ai-agent-rules` embedded in `ai-agents`), the

382: ## 2. Placement Rules
383: 
384: ### 2.1 New Skill Placement
385: 
386: 1. Match the new skill's topic keyword to a leaf group in §1.2.
387: 2. Place it in that leaf group (e.g., a new `git-commit-signing` skill goes
388:    under `git/basic/edit/`).
389: 3. If no leaf group matches the topic:
390:    * Create a new leaf group within the parent domain.
391:    * Verify the parent folder's item count stays ≤10 after addition (use
392:      `directory-tree-audit` if uncertain).
393:    * If the parent exceeds 10, propose and apply sub-grouping before adding.
394: 4. Sub-groups are flat leaves — a leaf group MUST NOT itself be sub-grouped
395:    unless it reaches ≥10 items.
396: 
397: ### 2.2 Cross-Cutting Skills
398: 
399: Skills that span multiple domains (e.g., `redaction-portability` applies to
400: all files, not just one domain) belong in `general/` — not in a specific
401: domain folder. If `general/` exceeds 10 flat items, create a sub-group.
402: 
403: *
404: 
405: ## 3. Change Protocol
406: 
407: ### 3.1 Adding a Group
408: 
409: * Add the new group to the tree in §1.2 with its item count.
410: * State the rationale in a `## Changelog` entry.
411: * Update every skill that references §1.2 (cross-reference sweep per
412:   `skill-factory` §5.1).
413: 
414: ### 3.2 Removing a Group
415: 
416: * Move remaining items to sibling groups or `general/` before removing.
417: * Remove the group listing from §1.2.
418: * Cross-reference sweep.
419: 
420: ### 3.3 Renaming a Group
421: 
422: * Update the name in §1.2.
423: * If the folder on disk is renamed, cross-reference sweep every skill that
424:   links to it via relative path.

# Git Submodule Commit Details — Agent Bridge

> **Skill Location:** `.agents/skills/git-submodule-commit-details/SKILL.md`

## When to Use This Skill

Invoke this skill whenever **complete submodule commit metadata** is
needed — regardless of what the metadata will be used for (rewording,
sync message composition, audit, etc.).

## Quick Reference

| Trigger Phrase | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| "extract submodule commit details" | Load skill, run Steps 1–6 |
| "get commit metadata from submodule" | Load skill, run Steps 1–6 |
| "what does this submodule commit contain?" | Load skill, run Steps 1–6 |
| "compose submodule sync commit message" | Load skill, pass output to `git_atomic_commit` |
| "reword submodule commit with full metadata" | Load skill, pass output to `git_submodule_commit_reword` |

## What This Skill Produces

A single structured record per submodule SHA containing:

1. Submodule path and SHA
2. Parent SHA(s) — merge-aware
3. Full commit message body (zero summarization)
4. File changes — additions, deletions, per-file classification
5. Author name, email, timestamp
6. Committer name, email, timestamp
7. Registration URL from `.gitmodules`

## Key Commands

```bash
# Step 1 — resolve pointer
GIT_PAGER=cat git -C <parent-repo-path> ls-tree HEAD <submodule-name>

# Step 2 — extract core metadata
GIT_PAGER=cat git -C <submodule-path> log \
  --format=format:"%P%n%an <%ae>%n%ad%n%cn <%ce>%n%cd%n%B" \
  <submodule-sha> -1

# Step 3 — file changes (regular commits)
GIT_PAGER=cat git -C <submodule-path> diff-tree \
  --no-commit-id -r --numstat <submodule-sha>

# Step 3 — file changes (merge commits)
GIT_PAGER=cat git -C <submodule-path> diff <parent1> <parent2> --stat

# Step 4 — classify added vs modified vs deleted
GIT_PAGER=cat git -C <submodule-path> ls-tree -r <parent-sha> | grep <filename>

# Step 5 — registration URL
GIT_PAGER=cat git -C <parent-repo-path> config \
  --file .gitmodules submodule.<submodule-name>.url
```

## Consumer Skills

- [`git-submodule-commit-reword`](../git-submodule-commit-reword/SKILL.md)
  — passes the record into the amended commit message
- [`git-atomic-commit`](../git-atomic-commit-construction/SKILL.md)
  — passes the record into submodule sync commit messages

Three failure modes have been observed when authors append rows carelessly: 521: 522: 1. **Unrelated skills listed**: a skill that neither composes nor consumes the base is added because its topic sounded adjacent. PROHIBITED — the table loses signal and downstream readers compose the wrong primitive. 523: 2. **Merely related skills listed**: a sibling skill that shares a topic but does NOT invoke / depend on / extend the base is added. PROHIBITED in this table — such skills belong in the base's `## Related Skills` section instead. The Composition table is reserved for true composers (callers that pipe through the base's public contract) and consumers (skills that hard-depend on the base's output shape). 524: 3. **Generic / non-contextual descriptions**: a true composer is listed but its description is a paraphrase of the composer's own one-liner ("does X with Y"). PROHIBITED — the description MUST state HOW the composer uses the base: which base section/script it invokes, what it pipes in, what it gets out, and (if applicable) at which stage of its own workflow. 525: 526: **Acceptance criteria** for any new row in `## Composition by Higher-Level Skills`: 527: 528: - [ ] The candidate skill ACTUALLY invokes the base skill (via script shell-out, explicit `§N` reference, or hard dependency on the base's output contract). If no such reference exists, the row is misplaced — move it to `## Related Skills` or delete it. 533: 534: (Persisted as `permanent_discipline.composition-table-membership-and-description-discipline`.) 535: 536: ### 5.2.2 Composition Rationale Section Discipline 537: 538: The `## Composition Rationale` section sits in the skill's front-matter zone (before `## 1.`) and answers a question the reader has on first arrival: **"why does this skill exist as a separate atomic unit, and how does it fit into the larger graph of skills?"** It is NOT a duplicate of `## Description` (which states what the skill does) and NOT a duplicate of `## Related Skills` (a flat list of adjacents). It is the **justification for atomicity + the upstream/downstream wiring statement**. 539: 540: #### Purpose by skill role 541: 542: - **Base skill** (owns a generic primitive consumed by others): Composition Rationale explains why the primitive was extracted as its own skill (typically: "multiple composers reuse it; inlining would split the SSOT") and names the known composer(s) that depend on its public contract. 10: # Agent Planning Rule: Core Principles and Best Practices
11: 
12: This document outlines the mandatory planning protocol for all AI agents. The primary directive is to ensure all
13: actions are preceded by a transparent, user-approved plan. This rule is foundational to establishing a clear,
14: trustworthy, and effective interaction model.
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## 1. Goal Description & Versioning
19: 
20: All implementation plans MUST follow a strict naming and header convention to ensure traceability and version control.
21: 
22: - **H1 Header Versioning**: Every implementation plan MUST use the format `# [Goal Description] (vN)`
23:   as its primary H1 title (e.g., `# [Setup Authentication] (v1)`).
24: - **Rule Compliance Reference**: A dedicated section titled `## Rule Compliance Reference` MUST immediately follow the
25:   H1 header. It must contain a bulleted list of the specific industrial rules (with relative links) being followed in
26:   the current plan.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. The Core Planning Directive
31: 
32: All agents must present a clear, step-by-step plan before any implementation. The plan must be explicit,
33: actionable, and tailored to the user’s request. **Only after the plan is approved or clarified should
34: implementation begin.**
35: 
36: This directive is not merely a formality; it is a critical safeguard. By externalizing the planning process, the
37: agent minimizes the risk of misunderstanding, prevents "hallucination," and ensures complete alignment with the
38: user's intent from the outset.
39: 
40: ### 1.1 Primary Goal Persistence Mandate
41: 
42: The agent **MUST** carry over the original 'Starting Point' enquiry (the core objective) into every version of the
43: implementation plan. This goal must remain the primary heading of the document. Any shift in focus or addition of
44: sub-tasks MUST be explicitly documented as secondary or supporting actions to this primary goal, not as a replacement
45: for it.
46: 
47: ### 1.2 Architectural Boundary Verification
48: 
49: Before adding any execution step, the agent MUST verify it is not designated as 'CI/CD Managed' in project rules.
50: Local execution of automated pipeline tasks is PROHIBITED. If a script is for CI/CD, the agent must only modify its
51: templates or source metadata.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. Components of an Effective Plan
58: 
59: An effective plan is built on four key pillars:
60: 
61: - **Clarity:** The plan must be written in plain, unambiguous language. Avoid technical jargon or internal thought
62: 
63:     process descriptions. Each step should be a simple statement of intent, easily understood by a non-technical
64:     user.
65: 
66: - **Step-by-Step Breakdown:** The plan must break down the request into a logical sequence of discrete, manageable
67: 
68:     steps. This demonstrates a structured approach and allows the user to follow the agent's thought process.
69:

101: # with the one-by-one mandate from §3.2.
102: PAGER=cat git submodule update --init --recursive <OWNER_REPO_PATH>
103: ```
104: 
105: - **Pedagogical Breakdown**:
106:     - `--init`: Initializes the submodule in `.git/config` if not already present.
107:     - `--recursive`: **Mandatory.** Submodules frequently embed their own submodules (the
108:       `powershell-scripts` submodule of `ai-agent-rules` is a real example). Omitting
109:       `--recursive` leaves nested pointers uninitialized and silently breaks any script
110:       that depends on them.
111:     - `<OWNER_REPO_PATH>`: Scopes init to the path just added in §3.2, preserving
112:       atomic failure detection.
113: 
114: #### 3.3.1 Fresh-Clone Bootstrap
115: 
116: When the **parent** repository is being cloned for the first time (not when a single
117: submodule is being added to an existing checkout), use the recursive clone form so every
118: level of the submodule tree materializes in one command:
119: 
120: ```bash
121: git clone --recurse-submodules <PARENT_REPO_URL>
122: # or, on an already-cloned parent that is missing submodule contents:
123: PAGER=cat git submodule update --init --recursive
124: ```
125: 
126: The agent MUST use the recursive form unconditionally — the cost of an unnecessary
127: recursion is negligible, while the cost of a missing nested submodule is a silent
128: runtime failure later.
129: 
130: ### 3.4 Branch Tracking Enforcement (Critical)
131: 
132: Per `git-submodule-rules.md`, the agent MUST NOT leave the submodule in a "detached HEAD" state.
133: 
134: 1. **Enter the Submodule**: `cd <OWNER_REPO_PATH>`
135: 2. **Identify Default Branch**: Run `git remote show origin | grep "HEAD branch" | cut -d ":" -f 2 | xargs` or assume
136: `main`/`master` based on inspection.
137: 3. **Checkout Branch**:
138: 
139:     ```bash
140:     git checkout main # or master, based on discovery
141:     git pull origin main
142:     ```
143: 
144: 4. **Return to Root**: `cd ..`
145: 
146: ***
147: 
148: ## 4. Verification & Commit Preparation
149: 
150: 1. **Verify Status**: Run `git status` to confirm the addition and pointer change.
151: 2. **Propose Commit**: Follow the atomic commit standard.
152:     - Message: `feat(submodule): add <OWNER_REPO_PATH> submodule`
153:     - Include: URL and purpose.
154: 
155: ***
156: 
157: ## 6. Traceability & Related Protocols
158: 
159: - **Parent Rules**: `ai-agent-rules/git-submodule-rules.md`
160: - **Naming Standard**: `ai-agent-rules/underscore-naming-rules.md` (if applicable) or `Underscore Naming Convention`
161: skill.
162: - **Session Log**: Document the addition in `docs/conversations/` if requested.

3: description: >-
4:   Convention for naming planning artifacts (task, implementation-plan,

8: ---
9: 
10: # Planning Artifact Naming Convention (v1)
11: 
12: This skill defines the naming convention for all planning artifacts
13: generated during AI-agent sessions. The convention embeds session
14: identity (human-readable name + machine-readable ID) directly into
15: each filename, ensuring artifacts are self-traceable to their source
16: conversation and sort chronologically at the filesystem level.
17: 
18: The convention was established during an OpenCode config preservation
19: session and generalised here for reuse across all agent workflows.
20: 
21: ***
22: 
23: ## 1. Formula
24: 
25: ```text
26: docs/<date>_<session-id>_<session-name-slug>_<artifact-type>_v<version>.md
27: ```
28: 
29: All planning artifacts MUST be stored under `docs/` in the main
30: repository (per
31: [Traceability Portability Mandate](../../../../../ai-agent-rules/ai-rule-standardization-rules.md)).
32: 
33: ### 1.1 Part Reference
34: 
35: | Part | Required | Format | Example |
36: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
37: | `date` | Always | `YYYY-MM-DD` | `2026-07-03` |
38: | `session-id` | Always | Full opencode session ID (without `ses_` prefix) | `<session-id>` |
39: | `session-name-slug` | Always | Kebab-case of the opencode session name | `opencode-config-versioning-preservation` |
40: | `artifact-type` | Always | Kebab-case type identifier | `implementation-plan` |
41: | `version` | Versioned only | `v<integer>` | `v3` |
42: | Extension | Always | `.md` | `.md` |
43: 
44: ### 1.2 Separator Rule
45: 
46: - **Underscore** (`_`) separates every top-level part.
47: - **Hyphen** (`-`) is used only WITHIN a part (date-separator,
48: session-name-slug, artifact-type).
49: 
50: Correct:
51: 
52: ```text
53: 2026-07-03_<session-id>_opencode-config-versioning-preservation_implementation-plan_v3.md
54: ```
55: 
56: Incorrect (hyphen between parts — ambiguous boundaries):
57: 
58: ```text
59: 2026-07-03-<session-id>-opencode-config-versioning-preservation-implementation-plan-v3.md
60: ```
61: 
62: Incorrect (truncated ID, missing date, missing name):
63: 
64: ```text
65: <session-id>_task.md
66: ```
67: 
68: ### 1.3 `ses_` Prefix Handling
69: 
70: The opencode session ID natively starts with `ses_` (e.g., `ses_<session-id>`). The `ses_` prefix MUST be omitted from
71: the filename because the filename context already identifies it as a session ID:
72: 
73: - Correct: `<session-id>`
74: - Incorrect: `ses_<session-id>`
75: 
76: The full 26+ character ID MUST be used — NOT a truncated form.
77: 
78: Artifacts carrying AI-agent session IDs (any assistant or tool) are local-only; never commit them.
79: Committed documents MUST NOT reference them — explain the relevant context self-containedly (see skill-factory §2.2).
80: 
81: ***
82: 
83: ## 2. Artifact Types
84: 
85: ### 2.1 Registered Types
86: 
87: | Artifact Type | Versioned? | Purpose |
88: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
89: | `task` | No (live checklist) | Track progress of the current session's objectives |
90: | `implementation-plan` | Yes | Detailed step-by-step plan for executing a goal |
91: | `implementation-plan-<topic>` | Yes | Topic-scoped variant used when one session produces MULTIPLE independent implementation plans; `<topic>` is a kebab-case slug disambiguating the plan (e.g. `implementation-plan-acers-audit-history`). The version counter is independent per topic |
92: | `commit-preview` | Yes | Preview of commits to be executed |
93: | `walkthrough` | Yes | Post-execution record of steps taken and decisions made |
94: | `walkthrough-<topic>` | Yes | Topic-scoped variant used when one session produces multiple walkthroughs; `<topic>` is a kebab-case slug disambiguating the record (mirrors `implementation-plan-<topic>`) |
95: | `skill-creation-plan` | Yes | Sub-plan for creating a new skill |
96: | `skill-documentation-plan` | Yes | Sub-plan for enriching existing skills |
97: | `audit-log` | Yes | Record of an audit or inspection |
98: | `summary` | Yes | Session summary or retrospective |
99: 
100: New artifact types MAY be added as workflows evolve; each new type
101: MUST be registered here.
102: 
103: ### 2.2 Versioning Rules
104: 
105: 1. NEW artifacts start at `v1`.
106: 2. When content is updated, increment the version: `v1` → `v2` → `v3`.
107: 3. OLD versions are NEVER erased by creation of a new one. The old file
108:    remains alongside the new one by default; however a superseded
109:    version MAY be intentionally retired ONLY through the authorized
110:    path — coverage audit FULL + explicit user consent — via the composer
111:    [`planning-superseded-version-retirement`](../planning-superseded-version-retirement/SKILL.md)
112:    (macOS: `trash`, never `rm`).
113: 4. For `task` (unversioned), the file is edited in place — it is a live
114:    checklist, not a historical record.
115: 5. Different artifact types have INDEPENDENT version counters — an
116:    implementation-plan at v3 and its corresponding commit-preview at v2
117:    is valid.
118: 
119: ***
120: 
121: ## 3. Examples
122: 
123: The following files were created during the originating session and
124: serve as canonical examples:
125: 
126: ```text
127: docs/2026-07-03_<session-id>_opencode-config-versioning-preservation_task.md
128: docs/2026-07-03_<session-id>_opencode-config-versioning-preservation_implementation-plan_v3.md
129: docs/2026-07-03_<session-id>_opencode-config-versioning-preservation_commit-preview_v2.md
130: docs/2026-07-03_<session-id>_opencode-config-versioning-preservation_skill-documentation-plan_v1.md
131: ```
132: 
133: All four share the same session identity (date + session-id +
134: session-name-slug) and differ only in artifact-type and version.
135: 
136: ***
137: 
138: ## 4. Related Skills
139: 
140: - [`skill-factory`](../../../skill-factory/SKILL.md) — Consumes this naming
141:   convention when generating planning artifacts for new skills.
142: - [`markdown-generation`](../../../markdown-generation/SKILL.md) — Markdown
143:   formatting standards that generated artifacts must obey.
144: - [`planning-artifact-lifecycle`](../planning-artifact-lifecycle/SKILL.md) —
145:   Lifecycle management for planning artifacts (versioning triggers, CAM §7.1
146:   enforcement, deletion protocol). Companion base skill that covers *how to
147:   manage* artifacts once named.
148: - [`planning-version-coverage-audit`](../planning-version-coverage-audit/SKILL.md) —
149:   Mandatory coverage gate used before a superseded version may be
150:   intentionally retired (§2.2 rule 3).
151: - [`planning-superseded-version-retirement`](../planning-superseded-version-retirement/SKILL.md) —
152:   Composer owning the authorized retirement path (coverage FULL + user
153:   consent; macOS `trash`, never `rm`).
154: 
155: ***
156: 
157: ## 5. Traceability
158: 
159: - Created: 2026-07-03

161:   separators, omission of `ses_` prefix, date prefix for task files, independent versioning for artifact types.

8: # Git Submodule Pointer Repair Skill (v1)
9: 
10: This skill provide surgical, high-fidelity repair of invalid submodule pointers within a parent repository's history. It
11: implements the **Synchronization Horizon** algorithm to autonomously identify the correct architectural alignment point
12: between parent mandates and modular history.
13: 
14: ***
15: 
16: ## 1. Environment & Dependencies
17: 
18: The agent MUST verify the following tools are available before execution:
19: 
20: - **Git**: Mandatory for repository operations.
21: - **Python 3**: Mandatory for the `repair.py` synchronization engine.

# Git Ref Content Audit — Skill Bridge

This file is a thin pointer. The active source-of-truth is [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md).

## When to use

Apply [`git-ref-content-audit`](SKILL.md) when you need to verify, file-by-file, that
every path captured by one Git ref (most often a stash with an untracked tree) is
present byte-identically in another ref (most often `HEAD`). Produces an
IDENTICAL / DIFFERENT / MISSING classification and a disposition verdict.

## Trigger phrases

- "Is this stash safe to drop?"
- "Has commit X been fully absorbed into branch Y?"
- "Compare every file in stash@{N} with HEAD."
- "Verify supersession before retiring this backup branch."

## Quick-start

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/git-ref-content-audit/scripts/audit-ref-content.py \
    --repo /path/to/repo \
    --stash "<message substring or index or stash@{N}>" \
    --show-diffs

For ref-vs-ref (no stash):

```bash
python3 .agents/skills/git-ref-content-audit/scripts/audit-ref-content.py \
    --repo /path/to/repo \
    --ref-a <commit-or-branch> \
    --ref-b <commit-or-branch>
```

See [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md) for the full procedure, exit codes, and the disposition matrix.
